name: Sherlock

field_reviews.reason: Official repo (github.com/sherlock-project/sherlock, ~89.7k stars) and its CLI usage/flags show no authentication or credential concept at all — it is a local Python CLI queried against target sites.
No auth exists anywhere in the official CLI docs; flags are search/output/proxy options only.
Free open-source install via pipx/pip (sherlock-project on PyPI) or the official Docker image; Bellingcat's live tool page independently confirms one-command install and purely local CLI operation.
No hosted API surface exists; Bellingcat's review states there is no official Sherlock API and the experimental REST API has been unmaintained since 2021.
No remote protocol offered by the project; CLI only.

The core claim is correct — the sherlock-project org publishes no MCP server, there is no vendor/hosted service, and no Composio toolkit exists — but the draft attached no evidence URL for this claim. Also incomplete: small community MCP wrappers do exist (e.g. github.com/Burnsedia/sherlock-mcp, a FastMCP wrapper exposing search_username, and the adeze/sherlock fork bundling an MCP server). These are low-adoption projects, so whether they meet the 'reputable_community_mcp' bar is a judgment call; none_found for official/reputable MCPs remains defensible.

Fair and cautiously phrased for a hosted-API integration pipeline: there is no remote interface, no credentials, and no official API to integrate against (Bellingcat: 'There is no official Sherlock API... running Sherlock locally... remains the recommended method'). However the tool demonstrably CAN be wrapped — community MCP servers and a paid Apify Actor already do so — and the draft itself acknowledges this in its uncertainty notes. 'not_buildable' is accurate under a no-remote-interface definition but overstates impossibility if local CLI/MCP wrapping counts as buildable.
Exactly right: the sole blocker is that Sherlock is a local CLI with no hosted endpoint; nothing about auth, pricing, or partnership applies.

notes: Re-checked the official GitHub repo, Bellingcat's independent tool review (live gitbook version), and searched for Sherlock MCP servers. The negative claims hold: no official API, no vendor MCP, no Composio toolkit. Nuances recorded: community MCP wrappers (Burnsedia/sherlock-mcp, adeze/sherlock fork) prove local wrapping is feasible, so not_buildable is fair only under a hosted-API definition — which the draft's own notes make clear. mcp_status lacked an evidence URL in the draft; replacement supplied. Beware an unrelated 'Sherlock MCP Server' by Covertlabs (infostealer intel platform) — different product, same name.
